mainTopic: The end of the משנה on groups who lose עולם הבא, and the גמרא's long discussion of דור המבול and נח.
overview: The amud opens at the end of the משנה's list of groups who lose עולם הבא. רבי נחמיה says אנשי סדום, like דור המבול, will not even stand in judgment, and the חכמים answer that אנשי סדום will stand, among the wicked. The משנה then lists the מרגלים, and for דור המדבר and עדת קרח רבי עקיבא and רבי אליעזר disagree about whether they have a future. The גמרא then focuses on דור המבול: whether they will live again or be judged, and how too much blessing made them proud and led them to reject God. Several teachings show that their punishment by water matched their sin, and that robbery is what finally sealed their fate, even for נח, who was saved only because he found favor. The גמרא brings opinions on the word וַיִּנָּחֶם and on whether נח was great only compared to his generation, each with a משל. It explains why the animals died but the fish did not. It ends with נח warning his generation to do תשובה, and their mocking question about what was holding the flood back.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה reads the פסוק as covering both דור המבול and אנשי סדום
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה finishes quoting תהלים 1:5. He reads its first half as speaking about דור המבול and its second half as speaking about אנשי סדום.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...the wicked in judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous." "Therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment" means the generation of the flood. "Nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous" means the people of Sodom.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing רבי נחמיה's proof that neither דור המבול nor אנשי סדום will stand in judgment at all. He splits the פסוק into two halves, one half for each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה ruled that דור המבול will not stand in judgment, but אנשי סדום will still stand in judgment. רבי נחמיה goes further and says neither group will stand in judgment. Each half of the פסוק gives him one of the two groups.
steps.confusionAlert: This text begins in the middle of a פסוק. The first words of רבי נחמיה's quote ("על כן לא יקומו") appear just before this point, at the end of the previous page.

phrases.english: the wicked in judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the פסוק from תהלים 1:5. רבי נחמיה began quoting it just before this point.

phrases.english: "Therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment"

"Nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous"

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כֵּן לֹא יָקוּמוּ רְשָׁעִים בַּמִּשְׁפָּט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, both דור המבול and אנשי סדום will not stand in judgment at all.

steps.title: The חכמים answer that they stand only among the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי נחמיה's reading. The words 'nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous' only mean that אנשי סדום will not stand among the righteous. They will still stand among the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: They will not stand in the congregation of the righteous, but they will stand in the congregation of the wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי נחמיה's proof. They read the same פסוק in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה took the second half of the פסוק ("sinners in the congregation of the righteous") to mean אנשי סדום never stand in judgment at all. The חכמים point out that this phrase only shuts them out of the righteous group. So אנשי סדום will still stand in judgment, together with the wicked.
steps.whatToRemember: Both groups lose עולם הבא. In the משנה's ruling, דור המבול does not stand in judgment, but אנשי סדום do stand in judgment, among the wicked. רבי נחמיה says neither group stands in judgment at all.

phrases.english: They said to him: They do not stand in the congregation of the righteous,
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, answering רבי נחמיה.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי נחמיה's proof from the פסוק, not the fact that these groups lose עולם הבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק only keeps them out of the righteous group. It does not keep them out of judgment entirely.

steps.title: The מרגלים lose their share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the מרגלים have no share in עולם הבא. It proves this by splitting one פסוק into two parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מרגלים have no share in עולם הבא, as it says: "And the men who brought up the evil report of the land died by the plague before ה׳." "Died" means in this world. "By the plague" means in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to a new group, the מרגלים. It brings a פסוק to prove they lose עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said "they died." It also adds "by the plague," so the משנה reads that extra phrase as a second punishment. "Died" is their death in this world, and "by the plague" is losing עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: דור המדבר loses its share
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא and will not even stand in judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא and will not stand in judgment, as it says: "In this wilderness they shall be finished, and there they shall die." These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings up דור המדבר. This is the generation that left מצרים and was punished after the מרגלים. רבי עקיבא gives his harsh ruling about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two phrases, "they shall be finished" and "there they shall die." רבי עקיבא learns two punishments from this, like the double wording about the מרגלים. He adds that they will not even stand in judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: the generation that wandered in the desert
they do not stand in judgment

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: The generation of the wilderness has no share in the World-to-Come,
and they do not stand in judgment,
as it is stated: "In this wilderness they shall be finished,
and there they shall die."
phrases.notes: במדבר 14:35

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, דור המדבר has no share in עולם הבא and will not stand in judgment.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: דור המדבר are God's pious ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees with רבי עקיבא. He applies a פסוק about God's pious ones, who made a covenant with Him through a sacrifice, to דור המדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: About them the verse says: "Gather to Me My pious ones, those who made My covenant over a sacrifice."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the opposite view about דור המדבר. He brings a פסוק that praises them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דור המדבר made the covenant with God at הר סיני through offerings. So רבי אליעזר sees them as the "pious ones" whom God will gather to Himself. This means they do have a share in the future.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: About them it says:
"Gather to Me My pious ones,

phrases.notes: תהלים 50:5

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, דור המדבר are God's pious ones and will be gathered to Him.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: עדת קרח will not rise again
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that עדת קרח will not rise at תחיית המתים. He proves it from two phrases in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: עדת קרח will not rise in the future, as it says: "And the earth covered them", meaning in this world, "and they were lost from among the congregation", meaning in עולם הבא. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to עדת קרח. רבי עקיבא again rules harshly, using the same two-part reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "The earth covered them" describes how they were swallowed in this world. "They were lost from the congregation" is read as a second loss, that they will not come back at תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: destined to rise up (at the resurrection)

phrases.english: The assembly of Korach is not destined to rise up,

phrases.english: "and they were lost from among the congregation", for the World-to-Come.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: God brings עדת קרח back up
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disagrees again. He uses a פסוק saying that God brings down to שאול and also raises up, and applies it to עדת קרח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: About them it says: "ה׳ kills and brings to life; He brings down to the grave and raises up."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the hopeful view about עדת קרח, just as he did for דור המדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עדת קרח went down into the earth alive, into שאול. The פסוק says God "brings down to שאול and raises up," so רבי אליעזר reads it as a promise that they will come up again.
steps.whatToRemember: For both דור המדבר and עדת קרח, רבי עקיבא says they are lost, and רבי אליעזר brings a פסוק showing they are brought back.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: About them it says:
"ה׳ kills and brings to life;
He brings down to the grave and raises up."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, עֲלֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, God will raise עדת קרח up from שאול.

steps.title: דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי עקיבא's ruling that דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא. He proves it by splitting one פסוק into two parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא. The פסוק says "And He wiped out every living thing." That refers to this world. It also says "and they were wiped out from the earth." That refers to עולם הבא. This is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה with a ברייתא. In it, רבי עקיבא says דור המבול has no share in עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say the same thing twice: "He wiped out" and "they were wiped out." רבי עקיבא reads the repeat as two separate wipings. The first is death in this world, and the second is losing עולם הבא. This is the same split-the-פסוק method we saw for the מרגלים in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the flood in the days of נח
Every living thing, everything that exists

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:

phrases.english: The generation of the flood has no share in the World-to-Come,
as it is stated: "And He wiped out every living thing
that was upon the face of the ground."
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:23

phrases.english: "And He wiped out every living thing": in this world,
"and they were wiped out from the earth": for the World-to-Come,

steps.title: They will not live again or even be judged
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says דור המבול will not come back to life and will not even stand in judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: they will not live and they will not be judged. The פסוק says "My spirit shall not judge in man forever." That means no judgment and no spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a stronger ruling. דור המבול will not even be brought back to be judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the word יָדוֹן as coming from דין, judgment. He reads רוּחִי as the soul being given back. So the פסוק takes away both things: they get no trial and no return to life.

keyTerms.meaning: They will neither live again nor be judged
A word in the פסוק that he reads as "judge" (from דִּין)
"My spirit", the soul that God gives

phrases.english: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says:
They will neither live nor be judged,
as it is stated: "My spirit shall not judge in man forever"
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:3

phrases.english: meaning: no judgment and no spirit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי עקיבא's ruling: not only no עולם הבא, but no judgment at all
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דור המבול will neither be brought back to life nor judged.

steps.title: A second reading: their souls will not return to their bodies
steps.stepSummary: A second reading of the same פסוק: their souls will never go back into their bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "My spirit shall not judge" means that their souls will not return to their sheath, which is the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a different way to read the same words "לא ידון רוחי."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here יָדוֹן is read as coming from נָדָן, a sheath, like the case a sword goes into. The body is the soul's sheath. So the פסוק means their souls will never go back into their bodies at תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: "Another explanation", a second way of reading the same words
A sheath, like the case for a sword; here it means the body

phrases.english: Another explanation: "My spirit shall not judge"
means that their soul will not return to its sheath.
phrases.notes: The "sheath" is the body. The soul is pictured like a sword going back into its case.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״לֹא יָדוֹן רוּחִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different meaning for the same word יָדוֹן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The souls of דור המבול will never return to their bodies.

steps.title: Their own souls will burn them
steps.stepSummary: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסף says that even when souls return at תחיית המתים, the souls of דור המבול will burn them as if they were in גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מנחם ברבי יוסף says: even at the time when הקב״ה puts souls back into dead bodies, their souls will be harsh to them as if they were in גיהנם. The פסוק says: "You conceive chaff, you give birth to straw; your spirit is a fire that will consume you."
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא describes what will happen to דור המבול at the time of תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not say that their souls stay out of their bodies. Instead, their own soul becomes a fire that burns them. Even the time when everyone else comes back to life is painful for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment for the wicked

phrases.english: רבי מנחם, son of רבי יוסף, says:
Even at the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another picture of their fate at תחיית המתים: the soul returns, but as a punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At תחיית המתים, the souls of דור המבול will burn them like the fire of גיהנם.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on דור המבול: no עולם הבא (רבי עקיבא); no life again and no judgment (רבי יהודה בן בתירא); and souls that burn them (רבי מנחם ברבי יוסף).

steps.title: Their arrogance came from too much goodness
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says that דור המבול became arrogant only because of the great goodness הקב״ה gave them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: the generation of the flood became arrogant only because of the goodness that הקב״ה poured out on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from their punishment to their sin. It brings a ברייתא explaining what caused them to go bad, and it is setting up the list of פסוקים that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surprising claim is that their sin did not come from hardship. It came from too much blessing. Wealth made them proud.

keyTerms.meaning: He poured out, gave them in abundance

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל לֹא נִתְגָּאוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל טוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment of דור המבול to the cause of their sin
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The arrogance of דור המבול came from the abundant goodness הקב״ה gave them.

steps.title: Verses describing their easy, wealthy life
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a list of פסוקים showing how comfortable and wealthy דור המבול was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is written about them? "Their houses are safe from fear, and God's rod is not on them." "Their bull breeds without fail; their cow gives birth and does not miscarry." "They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance." "They sing with drum and harp and rejoice at the sound of the flute." "They spend their days in good things and their years in pleasures." "And in a moment they go down to the grave."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its claim by listing פסוקים about how good life was for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק shows a different kind of blessing. They had safety, healthy animals, many happy children, music and joy, and long, pleasant lives. Even their deaths were quick and painless. Nothing in their lives pushed them to turn to God.

steps.title: Their wealth led them to reject God
steps.stepSummary: Their success led them to tell God to leave them alone. They felt they did not even need Him for rain, since they had rivers and springs.
steps.simpleTranslation: That goodness caused them to say to God: "Go away from us; we do not want to know Your ways. Who is the Almighty that we should serve Him, and what will we gain if we pray to Him?" They said: Do we need Him for anything except a drop of rain? We have rivers and springs that supply us.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now shows the result of their wealth. They openly rejected God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the blessing to the sin. Because they had everything, they felt independent. The one thing God seemed to give them was rain, and they believed their rivers and springs made even that unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it caused": the goodness led to this
We pray to Him, plead with Him
We supply ourselves, get what we need

phrases.english: And that caused them to say to God:
"Go away from us,
we do not want knowledge of Your ways.
What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him,
and what will we gain if we pray to Him?"
They said: Do we need Him for anything
except for a drop of rain?
We have rivers and springs
from which we supply ourselves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִיא גָּרְמָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ לָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what the goodness from step 13 led to
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Their wealth made דור המבול feel they did not need God, not even for rain.

steps.title: Punished with the very goodness they abused
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה says that they angered Him with the goodness He gave them, and with that same thing, water, He will judge them, through the flood.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה said: With the goodness I poured out on them, they anger Me, and with it I will judge them. As it is stated: "And I, behold, I am bringing the flood of water."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with God's response. Their punishment matches their sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They were proud of their water: their rivers and springs. So God punished them with water, the flood. This is measure for measure: the very gift they used against God became the tool of their judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure for measure, a punishment that matches the sin (the idea behind this step)

steps.whatToRemember: דור המבול sinned because of too much blessing. They trusted their own water instead of God, so הקב״ה judged them with water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the punishment was specifically a flood, and it ties the end of the story back to the ברייתא's opening claim that their sin came from too much goodness.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
With the goodness that I poured out on them,
with it they anger Me,
and with it I will judge them,
as it is stated: "And I, behold, I am bringing
the flood of water."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:17

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: בַּטּוֹבָה שֶׁהִשְׁפַּעְתִּי לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives God's response to their claim in step 14 that they had their own water
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The goodness they abused, water, became their punishment through the flood: measure for measure.

steps.title: Sinned with the eye, punished with water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says דור המבול became arrogant because of their eyes, which look like water, so הקב״ה punished them with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: דור המבול became arrogant only because of the eyeball, which is like water, as it says, 'and they took for themselves wives from whomever they chose.' So He judged them with water, which is like the eyeball, as it says, 'all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the windows of heaven were opened.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a second reason for why דור המבול sinned. They sinned through their eyes, so they were punished with something like an eye: water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא before this said they sinned because of too much goodness. רבי יוסי says the root was the eye: they took any woman they saw and wanted. The punishment matches the sin, because the eye is round and wet like water, and a spring is called מַעְיָן, from the same root as עַיִן.

keyTerms.meaning: Springs or fountains (related to the word עַיִן)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is another example of the idea that God's punishment matches the sin (מידה כנגד מידה), the same idea as Step 15.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
The generation of the flood did not become arrogant
except because of the eyeball,
which is similar to water,
as it says: 'And they took for themselves wives'
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. בראשית 6:2.

phrases.english: from anyone they chose.'
Therefore He judged them with water,
which is similar to the eyeball,
as it says: 'All the fountains of the great deep burst open,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:11. מַעְיְנוֹת sounds like עַיִן, eye, which is part of the point.

phrases.english: 'and the windows of heaven were opened.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation of the sin of דור המבול and again links it to the water of the flood, alongside the ברייתא's 'goodness' reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דור המבול sinned through the eye, which is like water, so they were punished with water.

steps.title: Sinned with 'great,' punished with 'great'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out that the word רַבָּה describes both their sin and their punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: דור המבול sinned with 'great' and were judged with 'great.' They sinned with 'great,' as it says, 'And ה׳ saw that the evil of man was great.' And they were judged with 'great,' as it says, 'all the fountains of the great deep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן notices that the same word, רַבָּה, appears both when the תורה describes their evil and when it describes the flood waters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is again that the punishment matched the sin. Their evil was 'great' (רַבָּה), and the water that came up from the 'great' deep (תְּהוֹם רַבָּה) was their punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The deep (the waters under the earth)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
The generation of the flood sinned with 'great,'
and with 'great' they were judged.
They sinned with 'great,' as it says:
'And the Lord saw that the evil of man was great,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:5.

phrases.english: and they were judged with 'great,' as it says:
'All the fountains of the great deep.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:11, the same פסוק used in Step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל בְּרַבָּה קִלְקְלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another 'punishment matches the sin' teaching, this time based on a shared word instead of a shared image.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word רַבָּה ties their great evil to the great deep that flooded them.

steps.title: Three flood springs still exist
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says three of the hot springs from the flood are still around today.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: Three of them remained: the בלועה of גדר, the hot springs of טבריה, and the great spring of בירם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a side fact. Some of the boiling springs that opened during the flood never closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the last step spoke about the 'fountains of the great deep,' רבי יוחנן says three of those fountains are still open. He names three real places in ארץ ישראל where hot water still flows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Three of them remained:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the fountains of the great deep from the פסוק just quoted.

phrases.english: the Beloa of Gader,
and the hot springs of Tiberias,
and the great spring of Beiram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ מֵהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'fountains of the great deep' just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three of the flood's springs still flow: בלועה דגדר, חמי טבריה, and עינא רבתי דבירם.

steps.title: Mixing species before the flood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the פסוק 'all flesh corrupted its way' as meaning that different species were mated with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.' רבי יוחנן says: This teaches that they mated domestic animals with wild animals, wild animals with domestic animals, everything with humans, and humans with everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about דור המבול, and רבי יוחנן explains what 'corrupted its way' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'all flesh,' not just people, so רבי יוחנן reads it as including animals. The corruption was mixing species that should stay separate, even humans with animals.

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי הִשְׁחִית כׇּל בָּשָׂר אֶת דַּרְכּוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ״,
phrases.english: 'For all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:12.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
This teaches that they mated domestic animals with wild animals,
and wild animals with domestic animals,
and all animals with humans,
and humans with all animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הִשְׁחִית כׇּל בָּשָׂר אֶת דַּרְכּוֹ עַל הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק describing another sin of דור המבול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'All flesh corrupted its way' means they mixed species, including humans with animals.

steps.title: Everyone returned to normal except one bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא adds that after the flood all creatures went back to their own kind, except the תושלמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא says: And all of them returned, except for the תושלמי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר כהנא adds a follow-up to רבי יוחנן's teaching about mixing species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the flood, the creatures went back to mating only with their own species. One bird, the תושלמי, kept mixing with other species.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of bird that kept mixing species

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says:
And all of them returned,
phrases.notes: He means that after the flood, they all went back to mating only with their own species.

phrases.english: except for the tushlami.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא: וְכוּלָּם חָזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds what happened after the flood to the species-mixing described in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the flood all creatures went back to their own species except the תושלמי.

steps.title: Robbery is what sealed their sentence
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that although דור המבול did every sin, their fate was only sealed once they started stealing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And ה׳ said to נח: The end of all flesh has come before Me.' רבי יוחנן says: Come and see how great the power of robbery is. דור המבול did every sin, but their sentence was not sealed until they reached out their hands to steal, as it says, 'For the earth is filled with robbery because of them, and I will destroy them with the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where God tells נח the end has come, and רבי יוחנן learns from it how serious stealing is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that announces the end of all flesh gives the reason: 'the earth is filled with חמס.' רבי יוחנן notes that only חמס is named as the reason, even though they did every sin. So stealing is what finally sealed the decree.
steps.whatToRemember: דור המבול did every sin, but their sentence was sealed only because of חמס (robbery).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying stealing was their only sin. They did every sin; stealing is what made the decree final.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches how serious it is to steal from others: it can tip the balance even for people already guilty of everything else.

phrases.english: 'And the Lord said to Noah:'
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:13.

phrases.english: 'The end of all flesh has come before Me.'
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל חָמָס,
phrases.english: Come and see how great is the power of robbery,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל עָבְרוּ עַל הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: for the generation of the flood transgressed everything,
yet their sentence was not sealed against them
until they stretched out their hands in robbery,
as it says: 'For the earth is filled with robbery because of them,'
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק quoted at the start, בראשית 6:13.

phrases.english: 'and behold, I will destroy them with the earth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל חָמָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק and a new lesson: the special weight of חמס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Although דור המבול committed every sin, their decree was sealed only once they engaged in robbery.

steps.title: A second פסוק about the power of robbery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a פסוק from יחזקאל showing that robbery leads to total destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'Robbery has risen up into a rod of wickedness; nothing will be left of them, nor of their crowd, nor of their wealth, and there will be no mourning for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק to support רבי יוחנן's point that robbery brings destruction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, חמס becomes a 'rod' that punishes the wicked. The result is complete destruction: nothing remains of them, and no one even mourns them. This backs up the idea that robbery seals a terrible fate.
steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים, one in בראשית and one in יחזקאל, show that חמס brings complete destruction.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Robbery has risen up into a rod of wickedness;'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:11.

phrases.english: 'nothing from them, nor from their multitude,'
'nor from any of them, nor shall there be wailing for them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: הֶחָמָס קָם לְמַטֵּה רֶשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק supporting רבי יוחנן's teaching about the power of חמס.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that robbery is what brings final destruction
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 7:11, where חמס becomes a rod of wickedness that leaves nothing behind

steps.title: Robbery stands up like a rod and accuses the generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the יחזקאל פסוק: robbery stood up like a rod before הקב״ה and demanded that nothing remain of the robbers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: The פסוק teaches that robbery straightened itself like a rod, stood before הקב״ה, and said: Master of the World, let nothing remain of them, not their crowds, not any of them, and let no one mourn them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the פסוק from יחזקאל that the גמרא just quoted. He pictures robbery standing up like a stick and accusing the robbers before הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'החמס קם למטה רשע', meaning robbery rose up into a rod of wickedness. רבי אלעזר reads this as robbery itself standing up to accuse. The rest of the פסוק becomes robbery's demand: wipe them out completely, with no one left even to mourn them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
This teaches that it straightened itself like a rod,
phrases.notes: 'It' means robbery, the חמס from the יחזקאל פסוק in the last step.

phrases.english: and stood before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and said before Him: Master of the World:
"Nothing from them, nor from their multitude,
nor from any of them, nor wailing for them."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 7:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁזָּקַף עַצְמוֹ כְּמַקֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק from יחזקאל cited in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Robbery itself 'accused' the robbers before ה׳ and demanded their total destruction.

steps.title: Even נח's sentence was sealed
steps.stepSummary: Reading נֹהַּ as נֹחַ, the גמרא learns that נח was also sentenced to die with his generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even נח's sentence was sealed, as the פסוק says: 'and not נח among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads one word of the same פסוק in a new way. It learns that נח was also included in the decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's last words, 'ולא נה בהם', are read as if they said 'ולא נח בהם', which means 'not even נח among them.' This tells us that the decree of destruction covered נח too. This sets up the next step, which explains how נח survived anyway.

phrases.english: (And even on Noah the sentence was sealed,
phrases.notes: This line is in round brackets: some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: as it is said: "And not Noah among them.")
phrases.notes: The word נֹהַּ (wailing) is read here as if it were נֹחַ, Noah's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל נֹחַ נֶחְתַּם גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further teaching from the same פסוק quoted in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נח was also included in the decree of destruction.

steps.title: נח was condemned but saved by finding favor
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that נח's sentence was decided, but he was spared because he found favor in ה׳'s eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Even נח's sentence was decided, but he found favor in ה׳'s eyes, as the פסוק says: 'I regret that I made them, and נח found favor in the eyes of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל agrees that נח was condemned. It explains that he survived only because he found favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the order of the פסוקים. The words 'and נח' come right after 'I regret that I made them,' so נח was part of the group ה׳ regretted. The words 'found favor' show that he was saved by ה׳'s kindness, not because the decree did not include him.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: נח was included in the decree on דור המבול. He survived only because he 'found favor' in ה׳'s eyes.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל נֹחַ נֶחְתַּךְ גְּזַר דִּין,
phrases.english: Even on Noah the sentence was decided,
but he found favor in the eyes of ה׳,
as it is said: "For I regret that I made them
and Noah found favor in the eyes of ה׳."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:7-8. 'And נח' comes right after 'I regret that I made them,' so he was included.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אַף עַל נֹחַ נֶחְתַּךְ גְּזַר דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 24 with a ברייתא and explains how נח survived.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נח was condemned too, but he was saved because he found favor in ה׳'s eyes.

steps.title: רב דימי‎: ה׳ was glad He prepared graves
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק 'וַיִּנָּחֶם ה׳ כִּי עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ', רב דימי says ה׳ said: I did well to prepare graves in the earth for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'וַיִּנָּחֶם ה׳ that He made man on the earth.' When רב דימי came, he said: הקב״ה said, I did well that I prepared graves for them in the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about the flood and brings רב דימי's reading of it. He reads וַיִּנָּחֶם in a positive way: ה׳ was 'comforted.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי reads 'in the earth' as pointing to graves dug in the earth. So the פסוק means ה׳ was content that people could be buried. The next steps will ask how we know וַיִּנָּחֶם is positive here.

keyTerms.meaning: Was comforted, or regretted (the word can mean either)
When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.confusionAlert: The word וַיִּנָּחֶם is the center of the whole debate. It can mean 'was comforted' (positive) or 'regretted' (negative), and the two opinions disagree about which meaning fits here.

phrases.english: "And ה׳ was 'vayinachem' that He made
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:6. The word can mean 'was comforted' or 'regretted', and that is the whole question here.

phrases.english: man on the earth."
When Rav Dimi came, he said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I did well that I prepared
graves for them in the earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new פסוק about the flood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וַיִּנָּחֶם means ה׳ was 'comforted' that He had prepared graves in the earth for people.

steps.title: How do we know the word is positive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that וַיִּנָּחֶם has a positive meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב דימי's reading. It is setting up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually וַיִּנָּחֶם is read as 'regretted.' So the גמרא wants to know why רב דימי takes it as 'comforted' or 'pleased.'

phrases.english: From where is this implied?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב דימי's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What shows that וַיִּנָּחֶם has a positive meaning here.

steps.title: Comparing to יוסף comforting his brothers
steps.stepSummary: The same word is used when יוסף comforted his brothers, so here too it means comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is written 'וַיִּנָּחֶם ה׳,' and there it is written 'And he comforted them and spoke to their heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing the word to another פסוק. In that פסוק, the same root clearly means comfort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית 50:21 יוסף comforts his brothers, and the word there plainly means comfort. Linking the two פסוקים gives וַיִּנָּחֶם in our פסוק the same positive meaning, which supports רב דימי.

phrases.english: It is written here: "Vayinachem ה׳,"
and it is written there:
"And he comforted them and spoke to their heart."
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:21.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא ״וַיִּנָּחֶם ה׳״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The same word means comfort in the story of יוסף, so it means comfort here too.

steps.title: Other opinion: ה׳ regretted preparing graves
steps.stepSummary: Others say ה׳ said: I did NOT do well to prepare graves. They prove it from 'וַיִּנָּחֶם ה׳ עַל הָרָעָה', where the word means regret.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: I did not do well that I prepared graves for them in the earth. Here it is written 'וַיִּנָּחֶם,' and there it is written: 'And ה׳ regretted the evil that He spoke of doing to His people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that reads the same word the opposite way, as regret. It proves this with its own comparison to another פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמות 32:14 וַיִּנָּחֶם clearly means ה׳ regretted a planned punishment. Using that meaning, our פסוק says ה׳ regretted creating people only to bury them. Both opinions use the same method, a comparison of words, but each picks a different פסוק and reaches the opposite meaning.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of וַיִּנָּחֶם. רב דימי says ה׳ was comforted that He prepared graves (compare יוסף comforting his brothers). Others say ה׳ regretted it (compare שמות 32:14).

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
I did not do well that I prepared
graves for them in the earth.
It is written here: "Vayinachem,"
and it is written there:
"And ה׳ regretted the evil
that He spoke of doing to His people."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֹא יָפֶה עָשִׂיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the word explained in steps 26-28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וַיִּנָּחֶם means ה׳ regretted that He had prepared graves for people.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: נח was righteous only compared to his generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads בְּדֹרֹתָיו as a limit: נח was a צדיק compared to his own generation, but not compared to other generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'These are the generations of נח; נח was a righteous, wholehearted man in his generations.' רבי יוחנן says: in his generations he was righteous, but not in other generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about נח, and רבי יוחנן explains the word 'in his generations' as a limit on how great נח was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word בְּדֹרֹתָיו seems unnecessary. רבי יוחנן says it limits the praise: נח stood out only because everyone around him was so wicked. In a generation like אברהם's, he would not have been special.

keyTerms.meaning: Generations, offspring, or the story of someone's life

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying נח was wicked. He agrees נח was a צדיק. He is only saying how big a צדיק נח was compared to other generations.

phrases.english: "These are the generations of Noah;
Noah was a righteous man, wholehearted in his generations."
phrases.notes: בראשית 6:9. The words in square brackets fill in the rest of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
"In his generations": but not in other generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּדוֹרוֹתָיו, וְלֹא בְּדוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of וַיִּנָּחֶם to a new פסוק about נח's righteousness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בְּדֹרֹתָיו limits נח's greatness to his own generation only.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: נח would be even greater in other generations
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads בְּדֹרֹתָיו as praise: if נח was righteous even in a wicked generation, he would surely be righteous in a good one.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: 'in his generations' he was righteous, and all the more so he would have been in other generations.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש disagrees with רבי יוחנן and reads the same word as extra praise for נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש uses a כל שכן argument. Staying good among wicked people is the hardest test. Someone who passed that test would do even better among good people.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same word in the פסוק can be read as a limit or as praise. This is a classic מחלוקת about how to judge a person by their surroundings.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says:
"In his generations": all the more so in other generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: בְּדוֹרוֹתָיו, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בְּדוֹרוֹת אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same word that רבי יוחנן explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בְּדֹרֹתָיו is praise: נח would have been even greater in a better generation.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's parable for רבי יוחנן: wine among vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא compares נח to a barrel of wine in a vinegar cellar. It smells good there, but next to other wine it would not stand out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says: here is a משל for רבי יוחנן's view. It is like a barrel of wine kept in a cellar full of vinegar. There, its good smell is noticed. Somewhere else, its smell is not noticed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives a משל to help us understand רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine is נח, and the vinegar is his wicked generation. The wine only seems special because of the sour smell around it. The same is true of נח among his wicked neighbors.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says:
The parable for Rabbi Yochanan's view:
To what is the matter comparable?
To a barrel of wine
that was resting in a cellar of vinegar.
In its place, its smell spreads;
not in its place, its smell does not spread.
phrases.notes: 'Its place' means there among the vinegar. Somewhere else, near other wine, its smell doesn't stand out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי יוחנן's view from step 30 with a משל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נח stood out only in contrast to his wicked surroundings, like wine among vinegar.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא's parable for ריש לקיש: perfume in a filthy place
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא compares נח to a flask of perfume. If it smells good even in a filthy place, it will surely smell good among spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אושעיא says: here is a משל for ריש לקיש's view. It is like a flask of perfume lying in a filthy place. Even there, its good smell spreads. All the more so it would spread in a place of spices.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא gives a matching משל for ריש לקיש's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the filth is the wicked generation. A smell strong enough to be noticed through filth is a powerful smell. Among sweet spices it would be noticed even more. So נח's goodness was strong, not just relative.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says נח looked great only next to bad people, like wine among vinegar. ריש לקיש says נח was truly great and would shine even more among good people, like perfume that smells good even in filth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya says:
The parable for Reish Lakish's view:
To what is the matter comparable?
To a flask of perfume
that was resting in a place of filth.
In its place, its smell spreads,
and all the more so in a place of spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a matching משל for ריש לקיש, parallel to רבי חנינא's משל for רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נח's righteousness was real and strong, like perfume that is noticed even in filth.

steps.title: Why were the animals destroyed in the flood?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ה׳ wiped out every living thing. The גמרא asks why the animals were punished if only people sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And He wiped out every living thing that was on the face of the ground.' If people sinned, what did the animals do wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the מבול and asks a question about it. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishment normally comes because of sin. Animals don't sin, yet the פסוק says they were destroyed too. So the גמרא asks what justified their destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: Every living thing, all that exists

phrases.english: "And He wiped out every living thing
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:23

phrases.english: that was on the face of the ground."
If man sinned,
what did the animal sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָדָם חָטָא, בְּהֵמָה מָה חָטְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק about the מבול and opens a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why animals, which cannot sin, were destroyed along with sinful people.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה's parable: the wedding canopy
steps.stepSummary: Animals were created to serve people. When the people were destroyed, there was no purpose left for the animals, just as a father tears down the wedding canopy when his son dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: it is like a man who made a wedding canopy for his son and prepared all kinds of food for the feast. Some days later, his son died. The father got up and took apart the canopy. He said: 'Did I make all this for any reason except my son? Now that he died, why do I need a canopy?' So too, הקדוש ברוך הוא said: 'Did I create animals for any reason except for people? Now that people sin, why do I need animals?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 34 with a משל about a father, his son, and a wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals were not punished for their own sins. They were created only to serve people. Once the people were being wiped out, the animals had no purpose left, so they were removed along with them.

keyTerms.meaning: Did I... anything? (opening a rhetorical question)

steps.whatToRemember: The animals died in the מבול not because they sinned, but because they were created to serve people. Without people, they had no purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the animals sinned. It explains their destruction by the purpose they were created for, not as punishment.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha:
A parable: to a man who made a wedding canopy for his son
and prepared all kinds of food for the feast.
Some days later, his son died.
He got up and took apart his canopy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: כְּלוּם עָשִׂיתִי אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל בְּנִי?
phrases.english: He said: Did I make anything except for my son?
Now that he died, why do I need a canopy?
So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Did I create domestic and wild animals
for any reason except for man?
Now that man sins,
why do I need domestic and wild animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה: מָשָׁל לְאָדָם שֶׁעָשָׂה חוּפָּה לִבְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Animals were created only for people, so when people were destroyed, the animals had no purpose and were destroyed too.

steps.title: Only creatures on dry land died, not the fish
steps.stepSummary: The words 'on dry land' in the פסוק teach that the fish in the sea were not wiped out in the מבול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'Of all that was on dry land died.' This teaches that the fish in the sea did not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to what it just said: the animals died because of the people, but the fish in the sea survived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 35 explained why the animals were destroyed along with the people. Here the extra words 'on dry land' (בחרבה) show the destruction only covered creatures on land. Fish living in the water were left out.

phrases.english: "Of all that was on dry land, died"
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:22

phrases.english: but not the fish that are in the sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר בֶּחָרָבָה מֵתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the destruction of the animals discussed in steps 34-35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'on dry land' leave the fish out; they were not destroyed in the מבול.

steps.title: נח warns his generation: floating bodies and a lasting curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי דמן קסרי explains a פסוק in איוב as נח's warning: do תשובה, or your bodies will float on the water and your name will become a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי דמן קסרי explained the פסוק 'He is swift upon the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth.' It teaches that נח the צדיק used to rebuke the people and tell them: Do תשובה. If you do not, הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring the מבול on you and make your dead bodies float on the water like empty wineskins. That is the meaning of 'swift upon the face of the waters.' On top of that, people in every later generation will use you as a curse. That is the meaning of 'their portion is cursed in the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי יוסי דמן קסרי takes a פסוק from איוב and reads each half of it as part of נח's warning to his generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, 'swift (קל) upon the waters', becomes the picture of light, floating bodies. The second half, 'their portion is cursed', becomes the idea that the דור המבול would turn into a curse word for all later generations. This also shows that נח did warn the people before the flood came.

keyTerms.meaning: Rebuking; warning someone about their wrongdoing

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei from Caesarea expounded:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"He is swift upon the face of the waters;
phrases.notes: איוב 24:18

phrases.english: their portion is cursed in the earth"?
It teaches that Noah the righteous
would rebuke them and say to them:
Repent,
and if not,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא עֲלֵיכֶם אֶת הַמַּבּוּל
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring the flood upon you
and float your corpses on the water like wineskins,
as it is stated: "He is swift upon the face of the waters."
And not only that,
but a curse is taken from them
for all who come into the world,
phrases.notes: He means later people would curse others by saying something like 'may you end up like them.'

phrases.english: as it is stated: "Their portion is cursed in the earth;

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּמִן קֵסָרִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about the דור המבול, this time about נח's warnings to them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in איוב describes נח warning his generation: do תשובה, or your bodies will float like wineskins and your name will become a curse for all time.

steps.title: The end of the פסוק: they cleared a path through vineyards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reads the last words of the פסוק, 'he turns not by way of the vineyards,' as teaching that the people were clearing a path through vineyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: The end of the פסוק says 'He turns not by way of the vineyards.' This teaches that they used to clear a path through the vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי continues explaining the same פסוק and now reads its final words. This leads into a short back-and-forth between the people and נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יפנה can mean 'turn,' but here it is read as 'clear out' (מפנים). It describes what the people were busy doing while נח was warning them. That sets up their question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Turns, or clears out (read here as clearing)

phrases.english: he turns not by way of the vineyards"
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the same פסוק in איוב.

phrases.english: teaches that they would clear a path through vineyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִפְנֶה דֶּרֶךְ כְּרָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes reading the same פסוק from איוב that step 37 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last words of the פסוק teach that the people were clearing a path through vineyards.

steps.title: The people ask נח what is holding the flood back
steps.stepSummary: The people challenge נח: if a flood is really coming, what is stopping it?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to נח: So who is holding it back?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, the people answer נח's warning with a question. This sets up נח's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח has been warning them about a flood, but nothing has happened yet. So they ask why it has not come already.

phrases.english: They said to him: And who is holding it back?
phrases.notes: They mean: if the flood is coming, why hasn't it come yet?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וּמִי מְעַכֵּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The people respond to נח's warning from step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is stopping the flood that נח keeps warning about?

steps.title: נח answers: one dove must first be taken out
steps.stepSummary: נח explains that the flood is waiting because there is still one 'young dove' among them that he must take out first.
steps.simpleTranslation: נח said to them: I have one young dove that I must take out from among you first.
steps.whatsHappening: נח answers the people's question. The flood is held back until one special person is removed from among them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נח calls this person a פרידה, a young dove, meaning someone precious and pure. As long as that person is still among them, the flood waits. This shows the delay was not because the warning was empty.

keyTerms.meaning: A young dove or pigeon; here a picture for one precious, righteous person

steps.whatToRemember: נח warned his generation to do תשובה. They mocked him by asking what was holding the flood back, and he answered that one righteous 'dove' still had to be removed first.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: פְּרֵידָה אַחַת יֵשׁ לִי לְהוֹצִיא מִכֶּם.
phrases.english: I have one young dove to remove from among you.
phrases.notes: The dove is not a real bird. He means one special righteous person still living among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: פְּרֵידָה אַחַת יֵשׁ לִי לְהוֹצִיא מִכֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the people's question from step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The flood is delayed until one precious, righteous person, the 'dove,' is removed from among them.
